text:
The fault is most likely in M1, the NMOS common-source device. Its sensitivities dominate both failing specs (+20% in M1 raises f3db by 15.8% and GBW by 19.8%, while M2 barely moves either). The operating point is consistent with M1 being undersized: gm1 ≈ 15.1 × 120.3 µA ≈ 1.82 mS, and gm1/(2π·C_L) ≈ 580 MHz, close to the simulated GBW of 517 MHz. The output pole is therefore limited by a transconductance that is too low for the 500 fF load. M2 is a diode-connected PMOS load (gate tied to vout), so it sets the gain near 1 but has little effect on bandwidth, which makes it the second candidate.

This limits GBW (~517 MHz) and f3db (~497 MHz) at the 500 fF load. Restoring the intended width, roughly 1.5-2x larger, should bring gm1 and GBW up to spec.
